tagline.text: Open-air Mediterranean-style shopping complex in south Manila since 1982

location.label: Location
location.text: Corner of Commerce Avenue and Madrigal Avenue, Ayala Alabang, Muntinlupa

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season (mixed indoor and outdoor walking)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~2,500 (meals and transport, excluding shopping, per person for half a day)

children.text: Alabang Town Center (ATC) is an old shopping complex in south Manila that opened in 1982, an open-air mall with a Mediterranean-style courtyard, Corte de las Palmas, and a strip of outdoor restaurants. As the heart of the Alabang and Muntinlupa residential area, where many Koreans live, it lets you shop, eat, watch a movie, and even handle passport business in one place.
Alabang Town Center is a shopping complex in Barangay Ayala Alabang in Muntinlupa, south of Manila. Locals call it ATC or simply "Town." It began in

as a modest strip mall with a supermarket and two cinemas, which makes it one of the oldest shopping malls in Metro Manila. It was expanded several times, in 1994, 2007, and 2011–2012, and took on its current Mediterranean-style lifestyle center look. According to Wikipedia, its floor area is about 48,000㎡.

What sets it apart from other big malls is that it is not shut inside a single building. The Ayala Malls introduction page describes ATC as the only open-air mall south of Makati that blends natural elements into the setting. Restaurants and cafes with outdoor tables line the central courtyard, Corte de las Palmas, and you shop by walking between buildings, so it feels different from a mall where you only breathe air conditioning. At the same time, the Metro department store and supermarket, the Rustan's department store, and the cinemas mean rainy days are not much of a problem.

Alabang has long been home to many Korean and other foreign residents in the Philippines. Right next door are the gated, upscale residential area Ayala Alabang Village and Madrigal Business Park, and this whole area was originally Madrigal family land. In the early 1970s the Madrigal family and Ayala formed a joint venture to develop it as a planned district, and ATC serves that community as a place for grocery shopping, dining out, and meeting friends. So think of it less as a tourist attraction and more as a way to step into everyday life in south Manila.

It is also worth knowing that the owner has recently changed. In December 2025 Ayala Land sold its 50% stake to the Madrigal family, and soon afterward Rockwell Land announced it would acquire 74.8% of the operator, Alabang Commercial Corporation. In July 2026 it was reported that Rockwell had raised its stake to about 99%. Rockwell has announced a redevelopment over the next 5 to 10 years, and the first phase covers improving parking, reorganizing vehicle circulation, and adjusting the tenant mix. Parts of the complex may be under construction, so check the latest announcements before you visit.

This is the face of ATC, a Mediterranean-style courtyard lined with restaurants and cafes with outdoor tables. The lights come on in the evening and the atmosphere is pleasant, so it is popular for family dinners and gatherings. Wikipedia notes that Chili's, Jamba Juice, and Krispy Kreme opened here in 2012.

This pedestrian-only restaurant row opened in 2012 and sits near Corte de las Palmas. However, according to Wikipedia it was temporarily closed from August 3, 2026, and Rappler reported that parts of it would close for redevelopment. Check which sections are open before you go.

A department store and grocery built in 2011–2012 in a four-level building on the site of a former parking lot. The supermarket reportedly opened on August 11, 2012, and the department store on August 18. It has basement parking, which is handy when you have a lot of groceries.
The upscale Philippine department store Rustan's has a branch here. It is a good place to shop with a high-end department store feel, and a nursing room is also reported to be located here.

ATC has a cinema with screens 1 to 5 on the ground level of the new entertainment complex. Wikipedia says the cinemas became a Power Plant Cinema branch after the takeover, so check showtimes on site or in a booking app.

The fourth level of the Metro building is described as housing a Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) passport office. It is known as a place where foreign and Korean residents handle passport business along with shopping, but office operations and appointment rules change often, so check the DFA announcements first.

This parish, built in the 1970s, was already here when ATC opened in 1982 and is said to have served as the mall's anchor. Several Sunday Masses are held, so you can stop by before or after your mall visit.

An office building that opened in 2015 and is connected to the mall. It shares the parking facilities, and the upper level was listed as open 24 hours in a 2022 guide but has not been recently confirmed, so check ahead if you are collecting your car late.

items.title: Half-day course
items.subtitle: Enjoying ATC from lunch to evening

children.text: On weekdays it opens at
. Arrive at opening time and browse the Metro supermarket or Rustan's first while it is quiet.
Head toward Corte de las Palmas and have lunch at a restaurant with outdoor tables. It is hot at midday, so choose a shaded or indoor seat.
Walk through the department stores and shops, and if needed handle errands such as the passport office on the fourth level of Metro at the same time.
Rest at a cafe, or check the cinema schedule and watch a movie.
After sunset the courtyard lights come on and the mood changes. Have dinner at the outdoor restaurants, and leaving late helps you avoid the rush-hour traffic.
Because you spend a long time in one place, we recommend a relaxed schedule with breaks rather than chopping the time into small pieces.

items.title: Full-day Alabang area course
items.subtitle: A loop around ATC and its surroundings

children.text: Before the mall opens, have breakfast near your hotel and take a light walk around the church or nearby streets.
After ATC opens, shop and have lunch.
Travel by car or Grab to look around nearby Filinvest City or Festival Mall Alabang.
Return to ATC for dinner and head home.
From the Makati side, the usual route is to take SLEX (South Luzon Expressway), exit at Alabang, and head toward Alabang–Zapote Road. Traffic is heavy at rush hour.
From NAIA Airport, travel time by Grab or taxi varies greatly with traffic. Check the exact time on a map app that day.
You can take a bus bound for Alabang along EDSA, or transfer from the MRT at Magallanes to a southbound bus.

The mall terminal is described as being at the corner of Alabang–Zapote Road and Theater Drive, with taxis, UV Express, and buses. The RRCG P2P bus to Greenbelt in Makati ran, per a June 2024 guide, roughly 6 AM–9 PM on weekdays from ATC at ₱110 one way (₱88 discounted), but no source confirms the exact boarding spot or current timetable, so check with RRCG first.
Jeepneys run along the Alabang–Zapote service road. Routes and operations change often.
You can also take the PNR to Alabang Station and transfer to a jeepney or bus.
The public transport information comes from older articles, so check current routes on a map app and on site.

items.title: Getting around in and near the mall

children.text: You get around the complex on foot. There are many outdoor stretches, so you will want a hat and water during the day.
The Grab pick-up and drop-off point is described as the entrance on the Alabang–Zapote Road side. It may change because of redevelopment work.

It is a shopping mall and can be visited all year, but to enjoy the outdoor courtyard and restaurant row, the drier season is better. From November to May it is relatively comfortable to walk and pleasant to eat outdoors in the evening.
During the Christmas season at year-end the mall is crowded and parking is difficult. Weekday afternoons or just after opening are the quietest.

ATC has Western, Filipino, and Asian restaurants and cafes with outdoor tables. Chili's, Jamba Juice, and Krispy Kreme are known to have opened in Corte de las Palmas in 2012. The tenant lineup changes often and may change with the redevelopment, so check the directory or on-site signs.

For lodging, hotels cluster nearby in Filinvest City. Crimson Hotel Filinvest City Manila, Acacia Hotel Manila, The Bellevue Manila, Azumi Boutique Hotel, and Vivere Hotel are listed as nearby accommodations. Rates differ by season, so check booking sites.

For groceries, the Metro supermarket is the most convenient. If you are looking for Korean groceries or snacks, check the store directory, and if you do not find them, try other shopping areas around Alabang. For dessert after a meal, the cafes in Corte de las Palmas are a good choice. On busy weekend evenings seats may run out, so go early or choose a restaurant that takes reservations.
The Ayala Malls page lists hours as
on weekdays and
on weekends, but another guide gives the weekend closing time as 21:00. Hours may change after the takeover and redevelopment, so check the official channels.
Parking hours differ by zone. Madrigal Parking is reported as

, but the closing time comes from a 2022 guide, and the 24-hour opening of the Corporate Center upper level is also confirmed by only that one 2022 guide, so check with the on-site parking office for current hours. Some areas may be blocked during redevelopment.
Free Wi-Fi is reported to be available for the first hour.
The smoking area is reported to be the garden near McDonald's.
During rush hour, Alabang–Zapote Road and the SLEX Alabang section are extremely congested. In the late afternoon it is also hard to get a Grab.
Sunday church Masses are held several times, so the area in front of the mall can get crowded then.
For paperwork such as passports, check the DFA announcements and appointment rules first.
Keep bags and valuables in front of you and take basic precautions. It is relatively crowded on weekends.
Because of Rockwell Land's redevelopment, parking zones, vehicle routes, and some sections such as The Street may change or close, so check the latest announcements before you visit.
Ownership and operations are in transition, so tenants and business hours may change.
In 2012 there was an attempted robbery of a cash van near the mall. Do not carry a lot of cash.
Traffic congestion is severe, so allow plenty of time right before airport or long-distance trips.
There are many outdoor stretches, and rain can pour down suddenly in the rainy season.
The world-famous Bamboo Organ church is in Las Piñas, in the same south Manila area as ATC. Travel time varies greatly with traffic, so check it on a map app.
A planned district near ATC with hotels, offices, and shopping facilities. Check the travel time on a map app.
A gated residential area right next to ATC. Outsiders face entry rules, so it is difficult to enter for ordinary sightseeing.
Travel time between the airport and ATC varies greatly with traffic.
